authority.legal_name: Washington State Ferries (a division of WSDOT)
authority.geography_type: an inland sea (Puget Sound / Salish Sea) of deep channels, narrow passages and islands
authority.home_waters_label: Puget Sound and the San Juan Islands

mandate.summary: Washington State Ferries, a division of the Washington State Department of Transportation, is the largest ferry system in the United States - an essential part of the state highway system carrying ~24 million riders a year across Puget Sound and the San Juan Islands on 10 routes and 20 terminals.
current_priorities: Run the 20-terminal, 10-route network as essential marine highway infrastructure
Deliver the 2040 Long Range Plan - vessel renewal, terminal upgrades and service restoration
Electrify the fleet - the largest hybrid-electric ferry conversion in North America, with charging at up to 16 terminals (first five: Bainbridge, Seattle/Colman Dock, Clinton, Bremerton, Kingston)
Restore service to pre-pandemic levels and add passenger-only fast-ferry capacity

policy_targets.vision: WSF 2040 Long Range Plan; Washington state greenhouse-gas reduction & clean-transportation goals
policy_targets.decarb_note: WSF is converting its fleet to hybrid-electric and building shore charging at up to 16 terminals - the largest hybrid-electric ferry program in North America.
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling tier is a natural passenger-only complement to the auto-ferry electrification program: fast, low-wake hops on the high-demand commuter channels, opening frequencies the big auto boats can't run economically.

precedent.headline: WSF is the largest ferry system in the US - ~24M riders/yr, 10 routes, 20 terminals - and is already electrifying.
precedent.network: Routes incl. Seattle-Bainbridge, Seattle-Bremerton, Edmonds-Kingston, Mukilteo-Clinton, Fauntleroy-Vashon-Southworth, Pt Defiance-Tahlequah, Port Townsend-Coupeville, and the Anacortes-San Juan Islands network (Lopez, Shaw, Orcas, Friday Harbor).
precedent.note: Ferries are core highway infrastructure in Washington, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the commuter channels.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above WSF's auto-ferry backbone - fast, frequent, low-wake hops on the busy Seattle-side commuter channels (Bainbridge, Bremerton, Kingston, Vashon) that complement the electrifying auto fleet, plus quiet access on the wake- and orca-sensitive San Juan waters.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/wharves/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public-ferry stops; new/committed stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The flagship commuter channel - Seattle to Bainbridge across Elliott Bay; a fast passenger-only foiling layer above the auto ferry.
Seattle to Bremerton via Rich Passage; a long commuter channel where a fast foiling boat cuts the crossing sharply.
Edmonds to Kingston across the Sound - a heavy commuter run feeding the Kitsap Peninsula.
Short, very high-frequency Whidbey Island hop - ideal for fast, frequent foiling service.
West Seattle to Vashon Island; a dense triangle commuter leg.
Vashon to Southworth - the third leg of the Fauntleroy triangle.
Port Townsend to Coupeville across Admiralty Inlet - exposed water linking the Olympic Peninsula to Whidbey.
Anacortes into the San Juans toward Friday Harbor - quiet, low-wake, orca-sensitive island access through Thatcher/Rosario passages.

regional_links.note: WSF runs one international leg, Anacortes <-> Sidney BC (Canada). That is a cross-border route and is explicitly out of the core domestic proposal - far-future roadmap only.

links.note: Anacortes to Sidney, British Columbia is an international crossing - out of scope for the domestic proposal; listed only for completeness.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: The Sound carries deep-draft commercial traffic under Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service; every leg must respect the traffic-separation scheme and cross lanes at right angles.

The Salish Sea / San Juan waters have legally mandated vessel-distance and go-slow rules around endangered Southern Resident killer whales; geofence speed- and approach-limited zones, especially in Haro Strait and around the San Juans.
Rich Passage is narrow, current-swept and wake-sensitive (shoreline damage history); displacement / no-foil, strict wake limits through the passage.
Cattle Pass, Rosario Strait, Thatcher Pass and President Channel run strong reversing currents and back-eddies; hand-waypoint the marked channels and account for set.
Port Townsend-Coupeville crosses exposed Admiralty Inlet with strong tide rips; route the marked crossing and manage swell.
Naval Base Kitsap (Bremerton and Bangor) has security/exclusion zones; route clear of restricted naval waters.
The Sidney BC leg crosses into Canadian waters - excluded from the domestic proposal.

sources.what: WSF 2040 Long Range Plan (10 routes, 20 terminals, ~24.5M riders)
